title: Advance Notice of Financial Liability and Patient Charge Types — Wound Care Supply Program
content:
# Advance notice of financial liability and patient charges — Wound Care Supply Program

Compliance policy on when an item can be billed to the customer and on the charge types that may be posted to a customer's balance.

## The liability notice

When an item or quantity the customer wants is expected not to be paid by the payer — above the tier's allowance without supporting documentation, an item the tier does not cover, or a replacement before the payer's replacement interval — Larkfield supplies it billable to the customer only after the customer signs the tier's liability notice for that item and quantity before the ship date; the customer signs it personally, and no Larkfield representative can sign it for them.

## Tier provisions

- **Wound Care Original Medicare Program.** The notice is the CMS Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage (form CMS-R-131); the claim is still submitted to Medicare with the notice on file, and the customer becomes liable only for a line Medicare denies.
- **Wound Care Medicare Advantage Program.** No notice can make the member liable; the member becomes liable only for an item for which the plan has issued a pre-service organization determination denial, recorded as a prior authorization denial for that item.
- **Wound Care Self-Pay Program.** No notice applies, because every item is priced at the Larkfield cash price.

## Patient charge types

A patient charge is posted only as one of these charge types:

| Charge type | What it is |
|---|---|
| self-pay price | a self-pay refill at the cash price |
| standard shipping | a self-pay shipment below the free-shipping threshold |
| expedited shipping | a customer-requested expedite |
| non-covered item | an item or quantity covered by a signed liability notice, or by a Medicare Advantage organization determination denial, that the payer denied, charged at the Larkfield cash price of the units concerned |

## The non-covered item charge

A non-covered item charge requires a liability notice signed on or before the ship date covering that item and at least those units, or on the Wound Care Medicare Advantage Program the plan's organization determination denial for that item; without it the amount is Larkfield's write-off and is never billed to the customer.

## Cases (hypothetical figures)

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Commercial PPO tier; the customer signed the plan's liability notice for 20 units of item A6212 the day before the ship date; the payer denies those 20 units | non-covered item charge of 20 units at USD 7.15, that is USD 143.00 |
| Same denial, but no liability notice was signed | Larkfield's write-off; nothing is billed to the customer |
| Medicare Advantage tier; the plan issued an organization determination denial for the item; the payer denies the line | non-covered item charge at the cash price of the units concerned |
